articles.headline: Masthead and corresponding editors
articles.summary: Christian Recorder, Vol. VII No. 18, Philadelphia, Saturday May 4, 1867. Masthead: Rev. Elisha Weaver, Publisher, General Book Steward, No. 631 Pine Street. Corresponding editors: Baltimore Conference Rev. B. T. Tanner; Philadelphia Conference A. L. Stanford; New York L. Patterson; New England W. W. Grimes; Ohio Samuel Watts; Indiana McIntosh; Missouri M. M. Clark; California T. M. D. Ward.

articles.headline: Baltimore Annual Conference, fiftieth session (report)
articles.author: W. D. Harris
articles.summary: Report of the 50th session of the Baltimore Conference of the A.M.E. Church, Bishop Wayman presiding with Bishop Payne. Business included a Virginia provisional conference (J. M. Brown), B. T. Tanner's manuscript 'Apology for African Methodism', admission of candidates and probationers. Rev. Elisha Weaver, General Book Steward, read his report on the Book Concern and the Recorder. At the Missionary Anniversary speakers included Maj. Gen. Gregory, James Lynch (editor of the Recorder), the bishops, Corresponding Secretary Rev. John M. Brown, Rev. A. T. Carr of the South Carolina Conference, Rev. H. M. Turner (Georgia) and Rev. Mr. Woodlin of Brooklyn. Baltimore candidates and probationers (T. M. Cole, W. Derrick, P. Shephard, J. H. Spriggs, J. F. Sisson, A. Woodhouse and others) are text only.

articles.headline: Men of the Times
articles.author: Louis Stanton Day [VERIFY]
articles.summary: For the Christian Recorder. An address in praise of the 'men of the times' (Garrison, Lincoln and others). Non-local, devotional/political essay; signed Louis Stanton Day [VERIFY signature].

articles.headline: Bethel Church Parsonage
articles.author: Progress [VERIFY pseudonym]
articles.summary: For the Christian Recorder. The members of Bethel have taken up collections for a parsonage; the writer asks whether it would not be best to build the parsonage on the ground adjacent to the church. This ground belongs to the Corporation though leased upon ground rent to other parties. The lot running 72 feet east from the north-east corner of 6th and Lombard St. has not paid the church one cent of ground rent for eight or ten years. The church surroundings are a disgrace: old frame shanties; on the corner of 6th and Lombard the tavern is never closed; in the yard of the shanty next to the church a swing kept for hire, used on the Sabbath by lads who annoy the Sabbath-school. Urges the Corporation to repossess the ground and erect a handsome parsonage.

articles.headline: Editorial items: New church in Philadelphia; colored voters of New Jersey; Mrs. Harper; Sarah's Tent
articles.summary: Items: the M.E. preachers' meeting of Philadelphia considered a new (John Wesley, colored M.E.) church; a lot costing $3,500 with $2,700 needed. D. D. Butler of Camden presented a memorial to the N.J. legislature on behalf of 7,000 colored voters. Mrs. F. E. W. Harper lecturing at Charleston S.C. on 'The Colored Man as a Social and Political Force'. Rev. James B. Reeve(s) of Central Presbyterian called to the 15th Street Presbyterian Church, Washington.
people: of Camden, memorial to N.J. legislature
pastor, Central Presbyterian Church (Rev.) [printed Reeves; elsewhere J. B. Reeve]

articles.headline: Book notice: William Still's pamphlet on the city railway cars
articles.summary: Notice of William Still's pamphlet 'A Brief Narrative of the Struggle for the Rights of the Colored People of Philadelphia in the City Railway Cars', refuting slanders on the 'Car Question'. (Streetcar topic.)

articles.headline: Conference schedule: Philadelphia Annual Conference
articles.summary: The Philadelphia Conference to meet in Philadelphia, May 18th, Bishop Wayman presiding (from the published schedule of conferences).

articles.headline: Information wanted: Elizabeth Parrott; James Watson
articles.summary: Information wanted of Elizabeth Parrott, wife of Nelson Parrott [also printed Parrett], formerly of a Virginia court house town; address Nelson Parrett, care of Rev. Jacob M. Mitchell, 613 Lombard st., Philadelphia (Apr 20-4t). Also of James Watson, who left Philadelphia in 1861 and shipped from Boston in the ship Lydia Scofield; his mother Jane N. Watson, Chester, Delaware Co., Pa., care of William Murphy (apr13-4t). Other information-wanted notices (Kentucky, Wilmington N.C., Millville N.J., Milton N.C.) are text only.

articles.headline: Marriages
articles.summary: April 25, by Rev. Jacob M. Mitchell, Mr. William C. Hooper to Mrs. Maria I. Stewart, all of Burlington, N.J. At Allentown N.J., April 28, by Rev. Peter Gardiner, Cato Dubois to Miss Edith Parker. On the evening of April 25, by Rev. J. B. Reeve, Mr. Amos B. Seynes [VERIFY] to Miss Mary B., daughter of James Clay [VERIFY] Esq.

articles.headline: Deaths
articles.summary: Eliza A. Butler, aged 45, died April 29, 1867; funeral from her husband's residence, No. 737 Kaighn's Point Avenue, Camden N.J., Saturday May 4 at 1 p.m. Rachel Wilkins died April 24, 1867, Camden N.J., of typhoid, consort of Daniel Wilkins, in her 55th year. Also an obituary of Louisa Hill of Wilmington, Del. (text only).

articles.headline: Directory of I. O. of Good Samaritans and Daughters of Samaria
articles.summary: Sheba Lodge, Juvenile I. O. of Good Samaritans and D. of Samaria, meets 2d Thursday of each month at 2 o'clock P.M. at Masonic Hall, South Eleventh Street; A. Cropper, F. O.; S. Young (printed YOUNO; clear as YOUNG on May 18), P. O. (Feb 23, 1 yr). Sumner and Wilson Lodge, No. 6, I. O. of Good Samaritans and Daughters of Samaria, meets second and fourth Thursdays each month at Masonic Hall, South Eleventh Street, Philadelphia, at 8 o'clock (apr 6 '67 1y).

articles.headline: Information wanted: Elizabeth Parrett (repeat, address variant)
articles.summary: Information wanted of Elizabeth Parrett, wife of Nelson Parrett, formerly of a Virginia court house town. Should Rev. Daniel Paine [sic] see this he will please address any information to Nelson Parrett, care Rev. Jacob M. Mitchell, 513 Lombard st., Philadelphia (April 20-4t). Other information-wanted notices (Eliza Silas of Prince George Co. Md. via New Bedford; Julia Grant of Wilmington N.C.) are text only.

articles.headline: Marriages
articles.summary: On the 2d inst., by the Rev. J. H. Reeve [sic], Mr. Peter H. Boardly to Miss Sophie King, all of this city. On May 2d, 1867, at Frankford, Pa., by Elder J. H. Smith, Mr. Alexander J. Bedford to Mrs. Rebecca J. Davis, both of Frankford. On April 25th, 1867, by Rev. W. R. Norris, Peter H. Tinson to Miss Margaret H. Hooper, both of Chester Co., Pa. By Rev. R. P. Gibbs: March 17, Mr. Norman Simmons of South Carolina to Miss Catherine Brown of Philadelphia; March 26, Mr. Jacob S. Hazlett to Miss Lydia Diton, both of Philadelphia; March 27, Mr. Benjamin Jones of South Carolina to Miss Hannah Bivons of Philadelphia; March 28, Mr. William Smith to Miss Elizabeth Winters, both of Philadelphia; April 2, Mr. John Diton to Miss Caroline T. Davis, both of Philadelphia; April 11, Mr. George W. Alston of North Carolina to Miss Sarah E. Williams of Philadelphia.
people: officiating minister (Rev.; printed J. H.; cf. J. B. Reeve May 4)

articles.headline: Rev. I. R. Gates' Macamoose: depot address changed
articles.summary: Rev. I. R. Gates' Macamoose, the great Indian remedy for the blood. Price $1.00 per bottle. For sale by druggists generally, and at the 'Macamoose' Depot, No. 613 Race street [VERIFY number], Philadelphia. (Earlier printings gave 1230 Wood St. and 1618 N. 11th; the depot address has changed.)

articles.headline: Country Boarding (Bucks County)
articles.summary: A pleasant country boarding house will open in Bucks County June 1st, 1867, three quarters of a mile from Schenck's Station. George Longstreth, proprietor, Bridge Water Post-Office, Bucks Co., Pa. (May 11-4t). Race of proprietor not stated.

articles.headline: Bone and Sinew for the Book Concern
articles.author: I. C. Wears
articles.summary: For the Christian Recorder. Proposes raising $50,000 for the Book Concern by issuing scrip in denominations from 25 cents to $5, redeemable in books, to be authorized by the General Conference.

articles.headline: Editorial items: Please Pay Up; Great Missionary Meeting; Sermon on Masonry
articles.summary: Please Pay Up: subscribers asked to remit to Elisha Weaver, Box 2975. Mr. Wears's plan for the Book Concern noted. The Board of Managers of the Parent Home and Foreign Missionary Society (Corresponding Secretary Rev. John M. Brown) to meet in Philadelphia. Sermon on Masonry by Rev. Theodore D. Miller, pastor of the Pearl Street Baptist Church of this city. Rev. Henry Davis in impaired health.
people: pastor, Pearl Street Baptist Church, Philadelphia (Rev.)

articles.headline: Death of Mr. James Mc. C. Crummell
articles.summary: Death of Mr. James Mc. C. Crummell [first name printed blurred, VERIFY] at his residence on Tuesday last (May 14, 1867); a dentist, also in the printing business; member of the Masonic and Odd Fellows' orders.

articles.headline: Personal items: Stephen Smith; Miss E. Handy; W. C. Banton; A. L. Stanford
articles.summary: Rev. Stephen Smith of our city chosen President at the Baltimore presentation of a portrait of Henry Winter Davis. Miss E. Handy, teacher of the colored public school at Kingsessing, bitten by a mastiff. W. C. Banton [VERIFY], superintendent of the Bethel Sabbath School, delegated to the State Sabbath School Convention soon to meet in this city. Rev. A. L. Stanford arrived from Savannah with his family; appointed to Ebenezer Church, Baltimore. 'Men of the Times' (May 4) was by Mrs. Lucia Stanton Day of Ohio.

articles.headline: Information wanted: Allen Valentine
articles.summary: Information wanted of Allen Valentine, formerly of Plymouth N.C. (sister-in-law Ellen Nickens). Address Rev. James U. [VERIFY surname], 1829 Addison St., Philadelphia (May 18-1t). Other notices (Jinkins of Bloomington Ill., Silas, Grant) text only.

articles.headline: Deaths: Mrs. Sarah Tady; Catherine Olive E. Leonard; Mrs. Mary J. Hooper
articles.summary: Mrs. Sarah Tady, born Baltimore 1788, came to Philadelphia at 16, married, later moved to Burlington N.J.; died April 24, 1867, aged 79 (signed Henry Davis). In this city, April 12, Catherine Olive E., youngest daughter of Rev. Chauncey and Mary A. Leonard, aged 6 years 10 months 28 days. April 26, 1867, Mrs. Mary J. Hooper, Treasurer of Sheba Lodge, Juvenile I. O. of Good Samaritans and Daughters of Samaria; the lodge resolved to drape its regalia for three months (signed A. Cropper and S. Young). Eliza Espeletta (Brooklyn) and Fannie Spriggs (Baltimore) text only.

events.name: Sarah's Tent (benevolent female organization) -- anniversary
events.description: Sarah's Tent, a benevolent female organization, held its anniversary on the 18th of last month (April 18, 1867) at Masonic Hall. Speeches by Mrs. Howard, Revs. Smith, Kinnard and Lynch, and Mr. Larence [VERIFY]. Surname-only speakers kept in text.

events.name: Colored People's Union League -- Grand Reunion Festival
events.description: PHILADELPHIA AFFAIRS: The Grand Reunion Festival of the Colored People's Union League was held on the 20th ultimo; reported by Mr. A. M. Green; eloquent speeches. Committee of Arrangements: Guy M. Burton, Thos. J. Bowers, Andrew F. Stevens, Jesse E. Glasgow, James W. Brown, Rev. Stephen Smith, Joshua D. Kelley, Benjamin Harrison, Thomas H. Davis, G. W. Gaines [VERIFY] and John C. Bowers.

events.name: Serenade to Hon. John W. Forney by colored citizens
events.description: On the evening of the 26th ultimo a delegation of colored citizens serenaded the Hon. John W. Forney at his residence, with a celebrated colored band, on the eve of his sailing for Europe. Address by O. V. Catto, Esq. (Parade/procession topic.)

events.name: Complimentary concert to Mr. A. Harris [VERIFY]
events.description: A complimentary concert to Mr. A. Harris [VERIFY surname], the renowned musician, at Liberty Hall last Monday evening (April 29). (Liberty Hall topic.)

events.name: Love feast at Bethel A.M.E. Church
events.location: Bethel A.M.E. Church, Sixth St., Philadelphia
events.description: Love feast at Bethel (Rev. James Hollen, pastor) Monday night last (April 29); itinerant ministers present included Revs. Mitchell, Gibbs, Weaver, Gould and James Lynch.

events.name: Union A.M.E. Church -- fourth quarterly meeting
events.location: Union A.M.E. Church, Coates St., Philadelphia
events.description: Notice: the fourth quarterly meeting of Union A.M.E. Church, Coates street, Sunday May 5, 1867. Ministers expected: Rev. Mr. Carr of Charleston S.C., Rev. T. H. Turpin, Rev. Elisha Weaver, Rev. W. D. W. Schureman. R. P. Gibbs, pastor [VERIFY, print blurred]. Dated April 29.

events.name: Wesley A.M.E. Church, Hurst Street -- fourth quarterly meeting
events.location: Wesley A.M.E. Church, Hurst street (Little Wesley), Philadelphia
events.description: Notice: the fourth quarterly meeting of the A.M.E. Wesley Church, Hurst street, May 12; love feast at 8. Wm. M. Watson, pastor. (Little Wesley per owner's ruling.)

events.name: Sociable Harvest Home for Rev. Mr. Boyer, Macedonia Church (Camden)
events.location: Mission school-house, Kaighnsville, Chestnut Street between Seventh and Eighth, Camden N.J.
events.description: Special notice: a Sociable Harvest Home for the benefit of Rev. Mr. Boyer, Elder of Macedonia Church, to be given by the ladies of Camden on Wednesday, Thursday and Friday, the 15th, 16th and 17th of May, at the Mission school-house, Kaighnsville, Chestnut Street between Seventh and Eighth. Admission single tickets 15 cents, season tickets 25 cents. Committee of arrangements, from whom tickets may be obtained: Mrs. Lows [VERIFY, possibly Laws], 246 Spruce street; Mrs. Oney, Mt. Vernon street; Mrs. Chase, rear of 407 Mt. Vernon street; Mrs. Clark, 246 Spruce street; Mrs. T. Hardy, 407 Mt. Vernon street; Mrs. D. Moce [VERIFY], Spruce street; Mr. D. Oney, 407 Mt. Vernon street; Mr. Gray, 407 Mt. Vernon street; Mr. Clark, Philadelphia. (Camden addresses; surname-only names not linked. Rev. Mr. Boyer is probably the G. E. Boyer of the May 4 Macedonia notice.)
attendees: committee of arrangements, 407 Mt. Vernon st., Camden

events.name: Wesley A.M.E. Church, Hurst Street -- grand rally
events.location: A.M.E. Wesley Church, Hurst Street (Little Wesley), Philadelphia
events.description: Special notice: a grand rally at the A.M.E. Wesley Church, Hurst Street, Sunday May 19th; all Christians and well-wishers asked to give twenty-five cents to five dollars 'to help us out of slavery' (the congregation is financially crushed). Bishop Wayman to be present all day with W. D. W. Shureman [sic, = Schureman] and other speakers. Agents holding subscription books asked to return them with monies that day. W. M. Watson, pastor (May 11-2t).

events.name: Wesley A.M.E. Church, Hurst Street -- fourth quarterly meeting, Sabbath appointments
events.location: A.M.E. Wesley Church, Hurst street (Little Wesley), Philadelphia
events.description: Fourth quarterly meeting May 12th; love feast in the morning, doors open 6 o'clock, service 8 1/2. Appointments for the Sabbath: Rev. T. Gould 10 1/2 o'clock, Rev. James Lynch 3 o'clock, Rev. George Boyer 7 1/2 o'clock. Wm. M. Watson, pastor (May 11-2t). The April 27 version of the notice is reprinted alongside. Adds the preaching roster to the May 4 entry.

events.name: Quarterly meeting at West Chester
events.description: The Christian public invited to the quarterly meeting at West Chester on the 3d Sunday in May (May 19). Love feast in the morning, doors open at 9; preparation sermon at 2 o'clock by Rev. D. Darrell [VERIFY]. Signed John Frisbee [VERIFY, small caps blurred], pastor (May 11-1t).

events.name: Complimentary concert to Mrs. Ferman at Liberty Hall
events.description: A Compliment to Mrs. Ferman: on the 8th inst. (May 8) a grand complimentary concert was given at Liberty Hall, Lombard street, to Mrs. Ferman by the Wilmington Band. Artists: Madam Brown, soprano; Mr. Mares, tenor; Mr. Morris, basso; Prof. Hazzard, pianist. Mrs. Ferman does business in the hall, which is in her care. (Liberty Hall topic; surname-only names not linked.)

events.name: Daughters of Cornish -- anniversary
events.description: The Daughters of Cornish, a female benevolent organization of about 200 members, Mrs. Carter President, to hold (or held) its anniversary at Liberty Hall this month; speeches by Revs. Stephen Smith, Allston, Weaver and Lynch. (Society meeting; Liberty Hall topic.)

events.name: Parent Home and Foreign Missionary Society of the A.M.E. Church -- annual meeting
events.description: Special notice: annual meeting of the Board of Managers, May 23d at 2 p.m., in the study of Bethel Church, Philadelphia, during the session of the Philadelphia Conference; anniversary meeting the evening of the 23d. Board by conference: Baltimore, Revs. R. Wayman, Wm. H. Hopkins, Wm. H. Waters; Philadelphia, Revs. Stephen Smith, Wm. Moore, E. Weaver; New York, Henry Davis, Deaton Dorrill, Joshua Woodlin; New England, J. P. Shreaves, John Barley, Ebenezer Williams; Ohio, James A. Shorter, John A. Warren, Jesse Devine; Missouri, W. R. Revels, Page Tyler, B. L. Brooks; Louisiana, Chas. Burch, John Turner, M. M. Clark; South Carolina, R. W. Cain, A. T. Carr, Wm. W. Brown; Georgia/Florida, H. M. Turner, C. H. Pierce, David Picket; Virginia, Geo. T. Watkins, J. R. V. Thomas, J. D. S. Hall; California, Thos. M. D. Ward. Robert F. Wayman, chairman; John M. Brown, corresponding secretary, Mission Rooms 84 North St., Baltimore; after May 16 care of Rev. James Lynch, Editor of the Recorder, No. 661 [sic; 631?] Pine Street, Philadelphia (April 27-tf). Only Philadelphia Conference members and bishops linked.
attendees: editor of the Recorder, forwarding address (Rev.)

events.name: Mount Pisgah A.M.E. Church, West Philadelphia -- grand rally
events.location: A.M.E. Mount Pisgah Church, Fortieth and Locust Streets, West Philadelphia
events.description: Special notice: grand rally at the A.M.E. Mount Pisgah Church, Fortieth and Locust Streets, West Philadelphia, Sunday May 26, 1867, to raise $1,000 toward a new church. H. J. Rhodes, pastor (May 18-1t). (Recorded as printed; not merged with H. G. Rhodes.)
